eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 2, Lesson 7
subtitle: What data we should expect from a process governed by chance.

steps.label: EXPERIMENT
steps.sub: Any process with an uncertain result

steps.label: SAMPLE SPACE
steps.sub: The set of ALL possible outcomes

code:
space = list(itertools.product(range(1, 7), repeat=2))
print(len(space))                          # 36

seven = [o for o in space if sum(o) == 7]
print(len(seven), len(seven) / len(space))  # 6  0.1667
caption: Six outcomes sum to 7 -- (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) -- out of 36 equally likely pairs.

eyebrow: The complement rule: P(not A) = 1 - P(A)
code:
one_six = [o for o in space if 6 in o]
print(len(one_six) / 36)      # 0.3056

print(1 - (5/6) ** 2)         # 0.3056  -- complement of "no six on either roll"
caption: The easy way to find "at least one six in two rolls" -- both routes agree.

eyebrow: The addition rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
caption: Mutually exclusive events (no overlap) simplify to just adding the probabilities.

eyebrow: The law of large numbers, by simulation
code:
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
r = rng.integers(1, 7, size=(n, 2)).sum(axis=1)
print((r == 7).mean())

# n=10: 0.2   n=100: 0.17   n=10,000: 0.1651   n=1,000,000: 0.1665
caption: Converging toward the exact answer, 0.1667, as the sample grows -- small samples wobble.
